genart.angiogenesis | genart | angiogenesis vasculature vascular capillary capillaries blood-vessel vessel microvasculature sprouting tip-cell filopodia anastomosis perfusion microangiography lumen blood-flow endothelium corrosion-cast india-ink doppler microscopy micrograph microscope fluorescence histology cell cells microbiology network branching pulsatile flow remodelling medical clinical genart generative fullbleed background organic eerie sublime menacing | - | A capillary bed under a fluorescence microangiogram, perpetually sprouting. Trunks branch across the field into ever-finer capillaries that meander and anastomose into loops, every vessel a lumen you can see the blood move through -- bright cells stream down each one on a pulsatile heartbeat. The bed is never finished: distal capillaries continuously sprout and regress, fading in and out on their own slow phases, and every terminal carries a migrating tip cell throwing out wiggling filopodia. Flow, pulse and remodelling all run on incommensurate rates so nothing converges. Offered as red microangiography fluorescence, India-ink perfusion, a metallic corrosion cast, or a false-colour Doppler velocity map.

genart.sarcomere | genart | sarcomere muscle striated-muscle skeletal-muscle cardiac myofibril myosin actin z-line z-disc i-band a-band h-zone m-line banding striation sliding-filament contraction ultrastructure electron-micrograph tem em polarised-light birefringence immunofluorescence microscopy micrograph microscope histology cell microbiology biology medical clinical wave stripes pulse genart generative fullbleed background clinical austere sublime | - | Striated muscle at the ultrastructure -- the sarcomere. Myofibrils stack across the frame, each a run of repeating contractile units read as the classic electron-micrograph banding: dark Z-lines bounding every sarcomere, light I-bands of thin actin, the dark A-band of myosin overlap with its lighter H-zone and central M-line. The muscle works: an activation wave travels along the fibres on incommensurate rates, so the sliding-filament mechanism plays out -- Z-lines pull together and the I-bands and H-zone narrow while the A-band holds its width -- a perpetual contraction and relaxation that ripples along the fibre and never re-phases. Offered as a grey transmission electron micrograph, polarised-light birefringence, Z-disc immunofluorescence, or a false-colour tension map.

The stomata work: guard cells swell and slacken with turgor so their pores open and close, each on its own rhythm plus a slow global light drive, while the chloroplasts stream inside and the whole peel drifts gently under the objective, everything on incommensurate rates so it never re-phases. Offered as a Nomarski DIC peel, confocal fluorescence with red chloroplast autofluorescence, an antique botanical plate, or a false-colour turgor map.
